messages:
jen_support: heads up — customer reported streaming responses stopping mid-stream and then a 500 from our edge. They say partial chunks arrive, then client sees connection reset. Happening on our chat SSE endpoint, low QPS. Logs attached by customer: `send() returned EAGAIN` several times, then `write failed: Broken pipe`. They included an nginx reverse-proxy in front of the client.
kevin_sre: can you paste the exact log lines and the request id? we need the route + model + auth scope. also whether this is hosted or Dedicated.
jen_support: request id r-8b3f4a, model redwood-1-large, hosted api, auth via API key, customer region us-west-2. customer's timeframe: around 14:02 UTC yesterday. their snippet: `2026-03-10T14:02:07Z send() returned EAGAIN (Resource temporarily unavailable) on fd 52, retrying` then `2026-03-10T14:02:08Z write failed: Broken pipe` then `2026-03-10T14:02:08Z aborting response after write error`
mira_runtime: thanks, that matches the code path where we short-circuit when socket write returns repeatable EAGAIN vs permanent EPIPE. normally we retry a few times and then drop. Did they have any client-side slow-consumer behavior?
jen_support: customer said their UI hung — they render each SSE line and the main thread blocks for ~200-500ms while processing UI updates. They also run a middleware that sets keepalive to 30s. They see partial frames like `data: {"delta":"...`" then nothing.
kevin_sre: this smells like backpressure — client is too slow to read, kernel send buffer fills, subsequent write returns EAGAIN. Our runtime currently treats repeated EAGAIN within 2s window as unrecoverable for streaming sockets (to avoid buffering unbounded). We then close connection to free GPU slots. That would cause the partial frames + abrupt close.
alan_oncall: any signs of this being caused by our edge or customer's nginx/proxy? Proxy buffering settings can exacerbate backpressure. If nginx buffers the response fully, it will itself block reading from upstream? worth checking.
jen_support: customer confirmed they have `proxy_buffering on` and `proxy_busy_buffers_size 8k`. They said switching to `proxy_buffering off` improved behavior in a quick test.
mira_runtime: interesting — if nginx buffers, it will read as fast as upstream writes until its buffers fill; then upstream writes see EAGAIN. So either we need to tolerate longer EAGAIN bursts or we should recommend disabling buffering or increasing `proxy_busy_buffers_size` for streaming endpoints.
kevin_sre: let's reproduce locally. I'll spin up a minimal SSE server that writes 1KB every 50ms and a client that sleeps 300ms between reads. I'll collect kernel socket stats.
kevin_sre: repro steps I used: ```bash
# server: simple netcat loop that writes chunks
while true; do printf 'data: chunk...\n\n'; sleep 0.05; done | nc -l 127.0.0.1 8000
# client: simulate slow read
python3 -c "import socket, time
s=socket.socket(); s.connect(('127.0.0.1',8000)); s.settimeout(10)
while True:
 data=s.recv(4096)
 if not data: break
 print('got', len(data))
 time.sleep(0.3)"```
kevin_sre: observed `send` on server started returning EAGAIN after ~2s, SO_SNDBUF at 0. Then after our server retried a couple times we forcibly closed socket. Repro matches customer.
mira_runtime: possible mitigations: 1) increase write retry window for streaming sockets and allow more transient EAGAIN (cost: memory/backpressure holding tokens). 2) add backpressure signaling header so proxies know not to buffer (e.g., `X-Accel-Buffering: no`). 3) provide guidance docs for customers: disable proxy buffering for SSE endpoints or increase buffersize.
alan_oncall: quick win: in the hosted control plane we can add a route-level header override to set `X-Accel-Buffering: no` for streaming routes. That would bypass nginx buffering at our edge and likely fix a bunch of cases. Any downsides?
mira_runtime: should be fine for chat/streaming ephemeral endpoints. Need to ensure we're not accidentally disabling buffering for large file downloads. We'll scope to routes with streaming response type.
kevin_sre: opened internal issue INF-8923 to track. Proposed short-term patch: extend EAGAIN retry policy from 2s to 5s for streaming responses and add a per-socket token cap of 512KB to avoid runaway memory use. Long-term: instrument per-connection send queue and auto-fallback to chunked smaller writes.
deploybot: deploy scheduled for canary tomorrow 02:00 UTC of edge config change (add X-Accel-Buffering header for streaming routes). CI: green.
jen_support: customer asked for repro steps to test their side: suggested curl test and a small python client. Example curl: `curl -N -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/sse?model=redwood-1-large\"` then have the browser/cli parse lines slowly.
jen_support: customer also wants a timeline — told them we have a canary planned and we'll follow up after monitoring.
kevin_sre: additional note — logs showed their client was Chrome-based with heavy DOM updates on each event. Recommend batching client render or using requestAnimationFrame to avoid blocking reads. We should add this to troubleshooting docs.
mira_runtime: I'll prepare a short RFC for the runtime change (EAGAIN window and token cap). Will include tests that simulate slow consumers and assert we don't OOM or leak sockets.
alan_oncall: marking this thread high priority until canary validated. :eyes:
jen_support: thanks team — will ping customer once canary is live and collect post-change logs.
kevin_sre: postmortem notes: root cause = slow consumer + proxy buffering + conservative EAGAIN policy. Fix = edge header + runtime retry tuning + customer guidance.
